title: Positive definiteness survives small symmetric entrywise perturbations
statement: Use the real field $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq0$ and let $G=(G_{ab})\in\mathbf R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric and positive definite, meaning $G_{ab}=G_{ba}$ and $\sum_{a,b=1}^n z_aG_{ab}z_b>0$ for every nonzero $z\in\mathbf R^n$. There exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that every real symmetric matrix $H\in\mathbf R^{n\times n}$ satisfying $|H_{ab}-G_{ab}|<\varepsilon$ for all $a,b$ is positive definite. The empty matrix is included, with the positivity condition vacuous when $n=0$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: If $n=0$, take $\varepsilon=1$. Every vector of $\mathbf R^0$ is zero, so the required positivity for nonzero vectors is vacuous for the unique empty matrix. Henceforth assume $n\geq1$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Equip $V=\mathbf R^n$ with $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_a x_ay_a$, and define $(Tx)_a=\sum_bG_{ab}x_b$. Coordinate vectors form a basis of size $n$, so $V$ is finite-dimensional. The inner product is positive on nonzero vectors since a sum of squares with a nonzero summand is positive. Symmetry of $G$ gives $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\sum_{a,b}G_{ab}x_by_a=\sum_{a,b}x_aG_{ab}y_b=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ after exchanging $a,b$. Thus [lem-sfb-real-symmetric-orthonormal-eigenbasis] supplies an orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ and real eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ with $Te_i=\lambda_i e_i$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Write $q_A(z)=\sum_{a,b}z_aA_{ab}z_b$ for any real matrix $A$. For every $i$, $e_i\ne0$ and $q_G(e_i)=\langle e_i,Te_i\rangle=\lambda_i$, hence $\lambda_i>0$. The minimum $c=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}\lambda_i$ of this finite nonempty list is positive. For $z=\sum_i t_i e_i$, bilinearity and orthonormality give $q_G(z)=\sum_i\lambda_i t_i^2\geq c\sum_i t_i^2$ and $\sum_a z_a^2=\langle z,z\rangle=\sum_i t_i^2$. Therefore $q_G(z)\geq c\sum_a z_a^2$ for all $z$.

source.place: Agent auxiliary to the Gram-matrix argument for lem-sfb-split-real-algebra-positive-squares. Milne II §1, Lemma 1.3, printed pp.77–78 motivates the rational algebra setting only; it does not assert this linear-algebra lemma. The agent argument is recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Set $\varepsilon=c/(2n)>0$, and let $H$ satisfy the stated hypotheses. Put $E=H-G$, $S=\sum_a z_a^2$ and $L=\sum_a|z_a|$. Expanding the nonnegative finite sum of squares gives $nS-L^2=\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}(|z_a|-|z_b|)^2\geq0$. Since $|E_{ab}|<\varepsilon$, the triangle inequality and distributivity give $|q_E(z)|\leq\sum_{a,b}|z_a||E_{ab}||z_b|\leq\varepsilon L^2\leq\varepsilon nS=(c/2)S$. Also $q_H(z)=q_G(z)+q_E(z)$ by expanding $H=G+E$. Consequently $q_H(z)\geq cS-|q_E(z)|\geq(c/2)S$. If $z\ne0$ then some $z_a^2>0$, so $S>0$ and $q_H(z)>0$. Together with the assumed symmetry of $H$, this proves positive definiteness with the same $\varepsilon$ for every $H$.
